text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.

- Sales of retail chains in Portugal would have stagnated or risen very little in 1996 if they had not opened new hypermarkets. Sales grew 10 percent in the year to September 1996, compared with 16 percent in the same year-ago period. The main reason for this trend is the restricted opening hours on Sundays, retailers say.

- Retail chain Jeronimo Martins plans to sell off up to two billion escudos of the assets of mineral water group Vidago, a source in Jeronimo Martins told the papaer. Jeronimo Martins recently announced a public offer to buy (OPA) Vidago.
- Banco Portugues de Investimento (BPI) plans to increase its capital with the issue of 10 billion escudos of perpetual debt denominated in Japanese yen, a BPI source said.

- Electricity group EDP-Electricidade de Portugal could hold up to 20 percent of shares in mobile phone operator Telecel if Telepri and Air Touch sell stakes, a source linked to the process told the paper.
- Canadian company Montemor Resources is prospecting for gold in the Alentejo region of southeast Portugal without government authorisation, the newspaper learned.
- The price of natural gas to be paid by Portuguese companies will be equal to the average paid in the European Union, according to a study by Transgas made available to the paper.
- Antonio Champalimaud plans to reorganise his financial services group under a new holding company Chemical Portugal SGPS, bank sources said.
- Manuel Carvalho da Silva, head of Portugal's biggest trade union group, CGTP, told the paper in an interview the government still does not consider job creation as a priority.
